transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um... I guess I'm here because... well, I've been trying to get on the lieutenant track at the firehouse. And part of that was just wanting to be in top shape, so I started eating cleaner. Just trying to be disciplined, you know? Which is a good thing, right? 

But... I guess it kind of turned into me, um, cutting my meals down a bit more than I probably should have. Like, lately I'll just do black coffee, a protein shake, and a pretty small dinner. And I'm doing that even on shift days, when I know for a fact I burned way more than that. I just... I want to make sure I'm approaching things the right way, I guess. Does that make sense? I hope I'm in the right place for this.
Are you worried about gaining weight if you eat more than you currently do?

Um, I wouldn't say "worried" exactly... I just want to stay sharp, you know? But... well, I guess if I'm being completely honest... yeah, maybe a little bit. 

Like, if the scale is up even just a single pound—maybe after a big station meal with the guys, or even just from drinking extra water—I get this... this tight panic. It's probably silly, I know. But it just feels like I’ve completely blown it, and I start worrying that the other guys are going to see me as soft, or like I'm just out of control of my own fitness. 

I know that probably sounds a bit extreme, doesn't it? I just really want to hold myself to a good standard for the lieutenant exam. Is it normal to get a little in your own head about that kind of stuff?
Do you think your weight or body shape is okay the way it is?

Um... I mean, I'd like to think it's okay. I'm definitely in better shape than I was, which is a good thing, right? 

But... I guess I do get a little fixated on it sometimes. Like, when I'm getting ready before a shift, I'll look in the mirror and... well, I catch myself really focusing on my waist, or checking if my face looks sharp enough. And if I feel like it doesn't... it kind of messes with me. It just makes me feel less confident, or less... command-ready for the day, I guess. 

I just want to look the part of a leader for the guys, you know? I hope that doesn't sound too vain. Do you think it's normal to tie your confidence to that kind of thing when you're up for a promotion?
Do you avoid eating certain foods because you're afraid of gaining weight?

Um... no, not really. I don't think so, anyway. I mean, I definitely try to eat clean, like I mentioned—sticking to proteins and veggies, that sort of thing. It's just about fueling the body right, you know? 

I wouldn't say I'm afraid of specific foods. It's more just... making healthy choices. Like, if the guys order pizza at the station, I might just have a salad instead, but that's just because I know the pizza will make me feel sluggish on a call. It's not out of fear or anything like that. That's just being disciplined, right? I think a lot of guys do that when they're training hard.
Do you think you would stop restricting your food intake if you reached your desired weight or body shape?

Um... yeah, I mean, I think so. Honestly, I haven't really set a specific "goal weight" or anything like that. It's more about just feeling ready for the exam. 

I'm sure once the lieutenant test is over and I've got the promotion, I'll probably relax a bit. You know, maybe join the guys for a burger after a shift without overthinking it. It's just a temporary push right now to make sure I'm at my absolute best. 

Once I feel like I've hit that standard, I don't see why I wouldn't just go back to a more normal routine. That makes sense, doesn't it? Like, it's pretty normal to dial things in temporarily for a big goal, right?
Do you feel like your eating habits and exercise routine are driven more by a desire to perform well as a firefighter or by a fear of what might happen if you gain weight?

Um... I mean, mostly performance, definitely. I want to be reliable for the crew and be at the top of my game. 

But... I guess... well, I hope you don't judge me for this, but maybe there is a little fear mixed in there, too. It's kind of embarrassing to admit, but if I step on the scale and it's up even just a pound—like, maybe just from drinking extra water or after a big meal at the station—I get this... this really tight panic. Like I've totally blown it, and suddenly people are going to see me as soft, or like I'm losing control of myself. 

I know it sounds a little intense when I say it out loud, but I just care so much about setting a good example for the guys. It's just because I want to be a good leader, you know? That makes sense, right?
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you're restricting your food intake?

Um... I guess... well, I wouldn't say it's the *main* reason. Like I said, it's mostly about the promotion and being a good firefighter. But... yeah, I suppose the fear is a pretty big part of it, too. 

I mean, I think I mentioned this just a second ago, but if I step on the scale and it's up even just a single pound—even if I know it's just from chugging water after a call, or having a slightly bigger meal with the crew—I just get this... this really awful, tight panic in my chest. It just feels like I've completely blown it, you know? And I start worrying that everyone is going to look at me and think I'm getting soft, or that I'm just totally out of control. 

I know that probably sounds a little crazy, letting one pound do that to me. I'm trying not to let it get to me that much, I really am. I hope you don't think I'm completely losing it for feeling that way. It's just... it's just a lot of pressure right now, right? Anyone would feel a little stressed about it, don't you think?
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is because of how you think you would look or because of how it would affect your performance as a firefighter?

Um... well, it's kind of hard to separate the two, honestly. I guess... I mean, I really hope this doesn't make me sound superficial or anything, but... it's a little bit of both? 

Like, when I'm getting ready for a shift and I look in the mirror, I... I guess I kind of fixate on certain things. Like, I check to see if my waist looks tight, or if my face looks sharp. And if I feel like I look... I don't know, a little puffy or soft, it just completely throws me off. It messes with my head, and I don't feel as confident or ready to take command that day. 

It's silly, right? Letting how my face looks dictate how I feel about leading a crew. But in my mind, if I look sharp and disciplined, it means I *am* sharp and disciplined, and the guys will respect me more. That's a normal way to look at it, isn't it? Like, wanting to look the part so you can act the part?
Is your fear of gaining weight mostly because you're worried about how you'll look?

Um... well, yeah, I guess I sort of just mentioned that, didn't I? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm answering you right. 

But, um, yeah... it is a lot about how I look, I suppose. Like I was saying, when I'm looking in the mirror before heading to the station, I just... I really focus in on my waist, making sure it looks tight, or checking if my jawline looks sharp enough. And if it doesn't... if I feel like I look a little soft or something, it just completely ruins my confidence for the whole shift. I just don't feel ready to take charge or command the guys if I don't look the part, you know? 

It probably sounds a little vain when I say it like that, worrying about my face and my waist. I'm really not trying to be superficial, I promise. It's just that looking disciplined makes me feel disciplined. That's... that's understandable, isn't it?
Is your fear of gaining weight mostly about how you think you would look to others?

Um... yeah, I guess that's a big part of it. I know I just talked about this, so I hope I'm not annoying you by bringing it up again. You're probably tired of hearing about it. 

But, um, yeah... it's just that when I look in the mirror before work, I really zero in on my waist and my face. I just need them to look, I don't know, sharp enough? And if they don't, if I look in the mirror and think I look soft or whatever, it just completely messes with how confident I feel. It's like I can't be command-ready if I don't look a certain way to the guys. 

I know it sounds really shallow to care so much about how I look to other people. I'm really not trying to be that guy who's obsessed with his reflection, I swear. It's just... I feel like they won't take me seriously if I don't look the part. Do you think that makes sense? Like, it's not totally unreasonable to want to look capable for your team, right?
Is your fear of gaining weight mostly about how you think you would look to yourself or how you think others would perceive you?

Um... well, it's honestly a bit of both, I think. I mean, I know I've been talking a lot about the guys and how they see me, and I hope I'm not overcomplicating things... I just want to give you the right answer. 

But, yeah, it definitely starts with me, you know? Like, when I'm looking in the mirror getting ready for a shift... I'm the one judging myself first. I'll focus right in on my waist, or check if my face looks sharp. And if I feel like I look soft to *myself*, it just ruins my confidence before I even step out the door. It makes me feel like I'm not command-ready, and then I worry that the guys will see that lack of confidence, too. 

So I guess it's like... how I see myself dictates how I think they'll perceive me? Does that make sense? I really hope I'm not sounding too self-obsessed or anything. I just want to be a good leader for my crew, and it feels like looking sharp is part of that. That's a pretty normal way to feel, isn't it?
When you're worried about gaining weight, is it more because of how you think you'll perceive yourself or how others will perceive you?

Um... well, it's a little bit of both, but I guess it really starts with me. I know I keep bringing this up, and I really hope I'm not sounding like a broken record or wasting your time. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

But, yeah, it's like... when I'm getting ready for a shift and I look in the mirror, I'm the one who's being hard on myself first. I always check my waist and my face, just to make sure everything looks sharp and disciplined. If I look at myself and think I look a little soft, it just completely throws me off. I lose that sense of being command-ready before I even get to the station. 

And then, because I feel that way about myself, I start worrying that the guys are going to notice I'm not at my best, you know? It's not that I think they're constantly judging my body, I just... I want them to see a capable leader. Does that make sense? I really don't want to come across as someone who's just obsessed with his reflection. I just want to do my job well, and feeling sharp helps me do that. That's okay, right?
When you worry about gaining weight, is it because you're afraid of how you'll see yourself?

Um... yeah, exactly. I know we're kind of circling back to this, and I'm really sorry if I'm not explaining it well enough—I promise I'm trying to give you what you need. 

But yeah, it really is about my own view of myself. Like I was saying, when I'm in front of the mirror before work, I just zero right in on my waist and my face. I really need them to look sharp. If I look at myself and think I look even a little bit soft, it just... it completely messes with my head. I lose that confident, command-ready feeling before the shift even starts. 

It's more about wanting to feel disciplined and prepared for the job rather than just obsessing over my reflection, you know? I really hope that makes sense. It's pretty normal to want to feel confident in yourself before going into a high-stress job, right?
Is your fear of gaining weight because you believe it would change your body in a way that you wouldn't like?

Um... yeah, I guess that's a big part of it. I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm totally fixated on the scale or anything... I know that's not healthy, and I'm really trying to just focus on being fit for duty. 

But... well, if I step on the scale and it's up even a pound—like, maybe after a big meal at the station, or if I just drank a lot of water—I get this... this really tight feeling in my chest. It's almost like a panic, like I've just completely blown it. I start thinking that my body is changing and that the guys are going to look at me and think I'm getting soft, or that I'm losing my discipline and just out of control. 

I know it's probably just water weight or whatever, and I shouldn't let it get to me... I'm really trying to be logical about it. But that fear of changing for the worse is definitely there. Is it normal to get a little worked up over that kind of thing when your job is so physical? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things to stay sharp.

Um... yeah, I suppose shape has a lot to do with it. I mean, I really hope I'm not coming across as vain or anything. I know we keep talking about this, and I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers. I just... I really want to be a good firefighter, you know?

Um... I think it's mostly for my own satisfaction, really. I mean, I know I mentioned the guys at the station before, and I do care about being a reliable part of the team, but... it's really about how I feel about myself.
